subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Ariane 5 Overflow
description: A quick, practical guide to Ariane 5 Overflow.

hook.text: Europe's new $7 billion rocket exploded 37 seconds after launch. The cause was a software type conversion error.

buildup.text: Ariane 5 reused navigation software from Ariane 4. It had worked perfectly for years. Why change it?

discovery.text: Ariane 5 was faster. A 64-bit velocity value overflowed when converted to 16-bit—the old code couldn't handle it.

twist.text: The overflow triggered a diagnostic dump that the flight computer interpreted as real navigation data.

climax.text: Both backup and primary computers ran identical code. Both crashed at the same moment. No fallback.

punchline.text: Reused code on a new system. Same test needed—but nobody ran it.
